executiveSummary: GM0537 passes the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract. Its 2025 CBS/PDOK identity, 67,089-person control, 42 neighbourhoods in seven districts, three BAG places, six BRT settlement labels, 64 scheduled-transit stop areas, zero conventional railway stations and four NWB road links are coherent; rounded neighbourhood rows differ by nineteen residents (-0.028%) and are correctly reconciled without rewriting observations. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Katwijk has a direct North Sea pathway, a primary dijk-in-duin/duin defence, Rijnland's largest boezem pumping outlet, dense coastal settlement and special dune-fire exposure. The coastal preset reports exactly 2.209121 m from T+6 through T+24, 38,423 affected people-equivalent and 687,230.352 deprived person-hours at T+24 without selecting a sea-level/gauge forecast, wave boundary, current defence state, breach/overtopping case, LIWO KatwijkaanZee footprint, probability, arrival or recession. It then sets direct water to zero at T+48 and labels T+72 recovering, although VRHM's official primary-breach scenario says water can penetrate the region within hours and recovery may not begin for weeks to months. Eight active presets reuse one neighbourhood order: Zuidduinen leads even for heat although the municipal stress test says the beach is cooler, while 't Heen-Zuid ranks second despite its different industrial/activity exposure. The major-river preset also emits 0.603709 m without a selected Rhine/Lek/IJssel or Oude Rijn–boezem mechanism. Public climate, groundwater, sewer, water-control, transport, care, utility, communications and external-safety sources can constrain the first 72 hours, but none establishes live state. Katwijk's public preparedness page asks households to self-support for 72 hours while local emergency support-point locations remain unpublished. Unknown, NoData, catalogue no-match and static register status must never be displayed as zero, open or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0537 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; full CBS features retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: Annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0537 as Katwijk in Zuid-Holland and reports 67,089 residents, density 2,704/km², 19.7% aged 65 or older and 8,924 one-person households; the generated centre [4.42056457552395,52.18740931762467] lies inside the 2025 boundary.

Forty-two neighbourhood rows in seven districts sum to 67,070 residents, nineteen below the municipality control (-0.028%); households sum to 27,540 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 13,175. Allocation reconciles to 67,089 without rewriting observations.

BAG supplies Katwijk, Rijnsburg and Valkenburg; BRT supplies five woonkernen and one buurtschap: Katwijk aan Zee, Katwijk aan den Rijn, Katwijk Noord, Rijnsburg, Valkenburg and De Pan. BAG/PDOK is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and CBS/BRT is CC BY 4.0.

The generated overview MultiPolygon has 91 coordinate positions. The fresh non-generalized service represents Katwijk as separate land and water features with 1,374 and 124 positions respectively; both are needed for source-faithful coastal analysis. Average home value covers 35/42 neighbourhoods, cars per household 34/42, doctor/supermarket distance 39/42, while district heat and charging cover 0/42; null and suppression remain NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Klimaatadaptatiestrategie en Uitvoeringsagenda 2021–2026, groundwater and wastewater context
evidenceSources.edition: Climate strategy 2021–2026; current groundwater and wastewater pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The municipal stress test says waterlogging is widespread and broadly comparable across the five main areas; Rijnsburg has many vulnerable residential and business properties. Rain can overload the sewer, make emergency routes impassable and discharge polluted overflow through the sea outlet, affecting coastal bathing water. These are official planning/stress-test conclusions, not observed depths or live road state.

The heat test identifies Katwijk aan Zee centre, Rijnsburg, parts of Valkenburg and Katwijk aan den Rijn, and business areas 't Heen, Kleij-Oost and FloraHolland as needing cooling; the document says the beach feels immediately cooler than the paved centre. Drought can affect water availability, foundations, subsidence, nature/fire and industry.

The current groundwater page distinguishes temporary high water after rain, poor clay/peat drainage, distance from ditch/outlet, subsidence, tighter replacement sewers and rainwater disconnection. It defines municipal public-space duties and private-parcel responsibility but provides no municipality-wide current groundwater observation or fixed machine feed.

The wastewater programme links Rijnsburg pumping and regional pressure mains to AWZI Katwijk, and the current 2024 wastewater ordinance requires 60 litres of storage per added square metre above its threshold. Static plans/design duties do not establish topology completeness, operating state, overflow, capacity, backup or restoration. No standard reuse licence or machine cadence was identified for these municipal documents/pages.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Kustwerk Katwijk, primary-defence register and Koning Willem-Alexander boezemgemaal
evidenceSources.edition: Kustwork completed 2015; primary-defence register last stated update 2023; current authority pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Kustwerk Katwijk moved the primary defence seaward and placed the centre behind a 900 m dijk-in-duin after the former alignment failed standards; 2.5 million m³ of sand widened the coast 80–100 m and the outlet canal was extended. This completed design context does not prove current strength, failure probability or selected breach.

Rijnland's current coastal policy says sea-level rise requires continuing space for dune growth; the effect at Katwijk's dijk-in-duin remains site-specific because the extended coast also erodes more strongly. The primary-defence legal register gives alignment, required dimensions and maintenance duties, was last stated updated in 2023 and is not a live condition layer.

The Koning Willem-Alexander boezemgemaal discharges the Rijnland boezem through the Uitwatering/spuisluices to the North Sea. Rijnland reports 94 m³/s pumping capacity and up to 75 m³/s additional discharge at high sea level; it is its largest of four boezem pumping stations and serves a region of more than one million people.

Capacity/design and registered status do not establish current pump/sluice availability, sea boundary, electricity/backup, salt intrusion, upstream storage, incident control or restoration. The public pages have no fixed machine incident cadence or standard redistribution licence stated.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Hollands Midden / Brandweer Hollands Midden
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2023–2026 and Regionaal Crisisplan 2024–2027
evidenceSources.edition: Regional risk profile 2023–2026; regional crisis plan December 2024 for 2024–2027; current Brandweer page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: VRHM identifies Katwijk and Noordwijk among the coastal locations where primary-defence failure is most plausible because dunes are narrow, while stressing that strengthening has occurred and failure needs an exceptional northwesterly storm and very high sea levels. In its EDO-coast scenario multiple coastal sections fail and seawater can move deep into the region within hours.

The profile distinguishes first indications around eight days ahead, sufficiently accurate coastal water/wave prediction around two days ahead and continued breach-location uncertainty through the last day. Impact depends on breaches, water height/duration, defence and road state; responders can have difficulty entering and people may self-support for days.

VRHM says recovery of services/infrastructure may not begin for weeks to months after primary failure and complete recovery may take years. Floodwater can become contaminated by industrial/transport toxic substances. These are official scenario statements, not a forecast, current defence state or Katwijk-specific depth.

The crisis plan defines notification, scaling, leadership, information, resources, communication and aftermath as core processes but relies on separate hazard/object plans for specifics. Brandweer Hollands Midden identifies the recreational Katwijk–Noordwijk dune/forest area as a special fire risk during dry periods. Public documents/pages have dated editions but no standard reuse licence or machine incident cadence stated.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — LIWO 2025 KatwijkaanZee candidate and timestamped coastal/weather observations
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO release 2025.1.6; Waterinfo and KNMI deployment snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: The public LIWO WFS bbox returns primary candidate 1524 KatwijkaanZee at [4.4040,52.2091] inside GM0537, with catalogue probability-band flags. The same query finds no regional, regional-water-system, outside-dike or supraregional-stress candidate point. A marker is an entry for selecting a professional scenario, not an active breach, selected footprint, forecast or probability estimate; empty categories do not mean safe.

No Waterinfo point is assigned inside GM0537. Scheveningen is nearest in the deployment cache at 14.54 km, observed 125 cm NAP at 17:30Z on 2 September 2026; forecast requests provide point values at T+1/6/12 but no local Katwijk point or complete selected T+72 coastal series. Point values are not wave conditions, defence state or inland depth.

No KNMI station lies inside GM0537; Voorschoten is nearest at 5.41 km and observed 18.4°C, 7.81 m/s gust and no hourly rain at 23:30Z on 2 September. That timestamped observation must not be aligned to the canonical synthetic storm without an explicit event clock and spatial-quality assessment.

Waterinfo is generally CC0, commonly ten-minute and public/non-mission-critical; KNMI observations are ten-minute CC BY 4.0. LIWO is versioned/irregular professional information with layer-specific resolution, units, coverage, NoData and licensing that must be retained and interpreted by water managers.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — NWB road gateways, RijnlandRoute/R-net, scheduled bus and timestamped road context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; GTFS version 9543 valid 30 August–12 December 2026; NDW snapshot 2 September 2026; current project pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The monthly CC0 NWB graph has four mobility/supply-only links: N206 toward Oegstgeest and Noordwijk, N434 toward Leiden and N441 toward Wassenaar. Both N206 sides share one physical corridor and nominal 150 values are non-additive synthetic units, not measured emergency capacity.

The N434/Corbulotunnel opened 5 July 2024 as the A44–A4 connection; it includes a roughly 2.5 km tunnel. Current R-net/N206 work adds bus infrastructure through 2026. These project descriptions establish geometry and project state, not incident-time tunnel, road or evacuation availability.

No conventional ProRail station is inside GM0537. OVapi GTFS version 9543, retrieved 31 August and valid 30 August–12 December 2026 under free-use/best-effort/no-SLA terms, assigns 64 stop areas. Schedule/geometry does not establish passengers, accessibility, vehicle availability, live service or emergency use.

The nearest NDW real record is 0.20 km from the reference point, a certain vehicle obstruction with unknown severity and no end time, versioned 15:14Z on 2 September. It does not prove any N206/N434/N441 route state at synthetic T+0; event-valid direction, footprint, expiry, destination and Unknown capacity must remain separate.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water assets, electricity planning, communications, education and acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: Public/deployment snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: Exact full-boundary assignment finds nineteen HWH points: nine sluices, eight surface-water pumps, one DWA/RWA sewer pump and AWZI Katwijk. HWH Kunstwerken is national/weekly and Waterketen DAMO contributor-dependent, both CC BY-SA 4.0. Records include boezem/outlet assets but do not establish connected topology, compatible unit, telemetry, live state, power/backup, condition or restoration.

One NBNL postcode sample at 2223VG maps to Liander area OS KATWIJK 10-2i and reports 44/22 MW existing/required withdrawal, a 7 MW/eight-request withdrawal queue, 84/3 MW existing/required injection, an 8 MW injection queue with request count null, twelve projects and earliest year 2026. At-least-quarterly/monthly planning is not full coverage, live load, outage, switching or spare emergency capacity; exact licence identifier was not found.

RDI assigns eighty antenna installations: 27 mobile, fourteen fixed-link, thirty amateur, two broadcast and seven other-mobile; its WFS states no reuse licence or cadence. Daily attribution-licensed DUO data assigns 42 education locations: 26 primary, five secondary, two special, one vocational/adult and eight other registered. Points do not establish radio coverage, occupancy, shelter role, backup or operation.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 CC0 assigns no acute-care point inside GM0537. LUMC in Leiden is nearest at 4.63 km straight-line and reports a 24/7 ED, acute obstetrics, seventeen rooms and 22,493 visits in 2025. Questionnaire values are not travel time, acceptance, staffing, occupancy, generator endurance or guaranteed capacity.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Katwijk / Rijkswaterstaat Register Externe Veiligheidsrisico's
evidenceSources.title: E08 — First-72-hour public guidance, transient activity and external-safety context
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal pages inspected 3 September 2026; 2017 environmental assessment retained as dated context; current REV/PDOK service inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Katwijk's current public guidance says immediate help may not be everywhere, households should prepare a package and plan for the first 72 hours, NL-Alert is the primary mobile channel and Radio West 88.0 FM/DAB+ 5B is the official emergency broadcaster. It says local emergency support points are still being developed and locations will be published when known.

Current municipal material reports many well-attended events; the annual Flower Parade is described as attracting more than 350,000 visitors. A recent municipal visitor-centre study estimates 1.8 million tourists annually but says detail is missing. These are aggregate/datetime-specific activity indicators, not incident-time occupancy or evacuation demand.

The dated 2017 municipal assessment identified the N206 dangerous-goods route and a cluster of hazardous-substance companies at 't Heen, including then-Brzo Chemische Industrie Katwijk. The current monthly CC0 PDOK INSPIRE Seveso point/polygon bbox query returns no match; that scoped no-match neither confirms the older status nor proves absence of other REV activities or hazardous materials.

The authoritative REV covers transport, storage and use of hazardous substances via API/WFS/WMS, with source authorities responsible for records. A causal incident needs a current activity/transport source, substance or effect class, issue/valid time, plume/flood interaction, protection/action advice, coverage and NoData; static older contours must not be treated as live releases.

residualLimitations: This audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a warning, forecast, hydraulic assessment, evacuation order, outage statement, route guarantee or operator commitment.
CBS 2025 values are rounded/suppressed and neighbourhood sums need not equal the municipality total; null statistics, capacity, monitoring, facility or forecast fields are Unknown, not zero.

The 91-position overview is for display/selection; analytical coast work needs both exact 1,374-position land and 124-position water features plus physical sea, beach, dune, defence, outlet, building and route geometry.
Kustwerk and the 2023 primary-defence register establish design/legal context, not current condition, breach probability or a selected event; LIWO candidate 1524 is not an active breach or footprint.
The VRHM EDO-coast description is an official extreme scenario, not a current forecast, universal local depth or claim that Katwijk's strengthened defence has failed.
Scheveningen Waterinfo and Voorschoten KNMI values are timestamped external points, not Katwijk inland depth, waves, defence state or canonical T+0; forecast gaps and no local point remain NoData.
Municipal climate, groundwater and wastewater evidence does not expose a complete current machine raster, parcel state, sewer model, overflow, bridge, route or restoration feed.
HWH's nineteen points and Rijnland's 94 m³/s design capacity do not establish connected topology, compatible register units, live pump/sluice/AWZI state, power/backup, salt constraint or dewatering.
NWB/NDW, GTFS, NBNL, RDI, DUO and RIVM records do not establish live passability, passengers, facility operation, physical utility topology, coverage, capacity, backup or repair.
No acute-care point lies inside the source coverage and public emergency support-point locations are not yet known; neither means care/support need is zero.
Registered residents omit beach/event visitors and business-park workers; aggregate annual/event counts are not incident-time occupancy, and buildings/businesses must not be converted into people.
The dated 2017 dangerous-goods/Brzo context and current Seveso no-match have different scope/time; neither establishes current complete REV inventory, live release, plume or flood contamination.
Direct earthquake zero, remote-smoke-only wildfire and empty catalogue/station queries are narrow model/source statements, not no seismic, ignition, smoke, access, drinking-water or supply risk.

Recovery beyond T+72, event lead time, cross-boundary water/service consequences, evacuation destinations, support/shelter/care capacity, mutual aid, staffing, crews and stocks remain outside locally validated scope.
